e150d.name: Caramel Class IV
e150d.description: Artificial coloring agent derived from heated sugars
health_effects: May contain 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI) - a possible carcinogen
Can cause digestive issues in sensitive individuals
Long-term consumption linked to potential liver and kidney concerns
e150d.why_harmful: Studies suggest 4-MEI, a byproduct of the caramelization process, may increase cancer risk with chronic exposure
e150d.environmental_impact: Low direct impact but energy-intensive production
e150d.alternatives: Use natural colorants like beet juice or turmeric

e211.name: Sodium Benzoate
e211.description: Chemical preservative used to prevent bacterial and fungal growth
health_effects: May cause hyperactivity in children, especially when combined with artificial dyes
Can trigger allergies or asthma in sensitive individuals
When combined with Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), may form benzene - a known carcinogen
May affect gut microbiome and nutrient absorption
e211.why_harmful: Can form benzene in beverages containing both sodium benzoate and ascorbic acid; linked to ADHD symptoms in children
e211.environmental_impact: Moderate - breaks down slowly in environment
e211.usage: Soft drinks, fruit juices, sauces, condiments
e211.alternatives: Use natural preservatives like salt, honey, or vinegar

e330.name: Citric Acid
e330.description: Natural acid often derived from citrus fruits, used to regulate pH
health_effects: Generally safe in small quantities
May cause tooth enamel erosion if consumed excessively
Can trigger sensitivity in people with citrus allergies
e330.why_harmful: Not highly harmful - mainly concerns are dental erosion and allergic reactions in susceptible individuals
e330.environmental_impact: Low - naturally derived or easily biodegradable
e330.alternatives: Already a natural ingredient; minimal need for alternatives

e331.name: Sodium Citrate
e331.description: Sodium salt of citric acid used as pH buffer and preservative
health_effects: Generally well-tolerated in small quantities
High sodium content may contribute to hypertension
Can cause upset stomach in sensitive individuals
May interact with certain medications
e331.why_harmful: Primary concern is sodium content; not recommended for those with high blood pressure or on sodium-restricted diets
e331.usage: Cheese products, processed meats, beverages, instant powders
e331.alternatives: Potassium citrate for those needing low-sodium option

e415.name: Xanthan Gum
e415.description: Polysaccharide produced from bacteria fermentation, used to thicken and stabilize products
health_effects: Generally recognized as safe by FDA
May cause bloating and digestive gas in some individuals
Can affect people with severe plant allergies
High consumption may slow gastrointestinal transit
e415.why_harmful: Mostly safe but can cause digestive discomfort; concern mainly for those with sensitive digestive systems
e415.usage: Salad dressings, sauces, gluten-free baked goods, ice cream
e415.alternatives: Gelatin, agar, guar gum for specific applications

e621.name: Monosodium Glutamate (MSG)
e621.description: Sodium salt of glutamic acid used to enhance savory flavors
health_effects: May cause 'MSG Symptom Complex': headaches, flushing, chest pain
Can trigger migraines in sensitive individuals
May contribute to obesity when consumed in high amounts
Linked to excitotoxicity - overstimulation of nerve cells
e621.why_harmful: Can over-stimulate taste receptors and potentially nerve cells; triggers adverse reactions in MSG-sensitive people
e621.usage: Instant noodles, soups, seasonings, savory snacks, Asian foods
e621.alternatives: Reduce salt, use herbs and spices for flavor enhancement

e202.name: Potassium Sorbate
e202.description: Potassium salt of sorbic acid used to prevent mold and yeast growth
health_effects: May cause histamine release in susceptible individuals
Can trigger allergic reactions and asthma attacks
Has been shown to damage DNA in cell studies
May affect nutrient absorption
e202.why_harmful: DNA damage observed in laboratory studies; can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals
e202.usage: Yogurt, cheese, dried fruits, beverages, baked goods
e202.alternatives: Use natural preservatives like salt, sugar, or vinegar

e310.name: Propyl Gallate
e310.description: Synthetic antioxidant used to prevent fat and oil rancidity
health_effects: Classified as possibly carcinogenic by IARC (Group 2B)
May cause allergic reactions and digestive issues
Linked to thyroid dysfunction
Can accumulate in body tissues
e310.why_harmful: Possible carcinogen; banned in several countries; potential to bioaccumulate in fatty tissues
e310.alternatives: Vitamin E (tocopherol), Vitamin C, rosemary extract

e320.name: Butylated Hydroxyanisole (BHA)
e320.description: Synthetic antioxidant used to prevent oxidation of fats and oils
health_effects: Considered a possible carcinogen (IARC Group 2A)
May disrupt hormone balance and endocrine function
Linked to respiratory tract tumors in animal studies
Can cause allergic responses
e320.why_harmful: Probable carcinogen; endocrine disruptor; banned in EU and Japan
e320.usage: Oils, fats, cereals, processed meats, chewing gum
e320.alternatives: Vitamin E, Vitamin C, rosemary extract, natural antioxidants

e321.name: Butylated Hydroxytoluene (BHT)
e321.description: Synthetic antioxidant similar to BHA, used to preserve fats
health_effects: Possible carcinogen (IARC Group 2B)
Endocrine disruptor - may affect hormone levels
Can cause hyperactivity in children
May damage liver and kidneys with chronic exposure
e321.why_harmful: Potential carcinogen; endocrine disrupting properties; banned in EU
e321.usage: Oils, gum, cereals, baked goods, fast food
e321.alternatives: Vitamin E, rosemary extract, ascorbyl palmitate

e250.name: Sodium Nitrite
e250.description: Chemical used to preserve meat products and give them pink color
health_effects: Reacts with proteins to form N-nitrosamines - potent carcinogens
Increases risk of colorectal cancer with regular consumption
May cause methemoglobinemia in infants
Depletes vitamin C in the body
e250.why_harmful: Forms carcinogenic compounds when combined with proteins; strong link to colorectal cancer
e250.usage: Cured meats, bacon, ham, hot dogs, deli meats
e250.alternatives: Use salt-curing without nitrites; choose uncured meats

e951.name: Aspartame
e951.description: Non-caloric artificial sweetener approximately 200x sweeter than sugar
health_effects: Contains phenylalanine - dangerous for people with phenylketonuria (PKU)
May increase appetite and promote weight gain despite zero calories
Linked to migraines and headaches in sensitive individuals
Metabolizes into methanol and formaldehyde in the body
Some studies suggest potential neurological effects
e951.why_harmful: Metabolizes into toxic compounds; brain accessibility questioned; unsafe for PKU patients
e951.usage: Diet sodas, sugar-free gum, artificial sweetened yogurt, diet desserts

e952.name: Sodium Cyclamate
e952.description: Non-nutritive sweetener banned in US but allowed in many countries
health_effects: Banned in USA due to cancer concerns
May cause allergic reactions and digestive issues
Potential liver and kidney toxin
Not suitable for children or pregnant women
e952.why_harmful: Banned in USA and 30+ countries; potential carcinogen and organ toxin
e952.environmental_impact: Moderate - persists in body and environment
e952.usage: Diet drinks, artificial sweetened products (mainly outside USA)

e129.name: Allura Red AC (Food Red 17)
e129.description: Synthetic red food dye derived from petroleum
health_effects: Can trigger hyperactivity in children
May cause allergic reactions and hives
Contains benzidine metabolites - potential carcinogens
May worsen ADHD symptoms
e129.why_harmful: Petroleum-based dye; linked to behavioral issues in children; contains potential carcinogenic metabolites
e129.usage: Soft drinks, candies, ice cream, processed foods, cosmetics
e129.alternatives: Beet juice, carmine, natural strawberry coloring

e104.name: Quinoline Yellow (Food Yellow 13)
e104.description: Synthetic yellow food dye commonly used in beverages
health_effects: May trigger allergic reactions including urticaria
Can cause hypersensitivity in asthmatic individuals
Potential reproductive and developmental toxin
Oil-soluble dye that concentrates in fatty tissues
e104.why_harmful: Can concentrate in body tissues; triggers severe allergies; questionable reproductive safety
e104.usage: Soft drinks, fruit juices, desserts, confectionery
